В этой игре мне не нравится только одно: она слишком длинная. Две или даже три главы можно было бы смело вырезать, и это сделало бы прохождение более динамичным и увлекательным. Специфика юмора и персонажей такова, что с ними легко переборщить, поэтому меньше всегда лучше, чем больше. 
Здорово, что есть отдельная опция для настройки уровня сортирного юмора. Я как высокодуховный интеллектуальный человек солидного возраста естественно выкрутила её на максимум и получила максимум эстетического удовольствия в полицейском участке, но к концу игры оно знатно приелось. Как и безграничное слабоумие протагониста. А ещё мне не понравились персонаж Каролины и её мамки, первая до бесячего раздражающая, вторая раздражающе скучная.  
Но это несущественные мелочи, общее впечатление об игре самое замечательное. Загадки отличные, веселые, диалоги и персонажи забавные, сюжет есть, офигенные мини-игры, местами гораздо веселее самого сюжета, кстати. Круто, что неписи запоминают твои предыдущие решения и обладают зачатками здравого смысла, что на моей памяти я встречаю в играх такого жанра впервые. Оставляет свежие впечатления.

Demetrios — это классический point-and-click квест старой школы, щедро приправленный циничным юмором, самоиронией и намеренной неловкостью.

Сюжет рассказывает о парижском торговце антиквариатом, который после ограбления оказывается втянут в цепочку странных и не всегда логичных событий. История подаётся легко, часто ломает четвёртую стену и регулярно шутит над самим жанром, игроком и происходящим на экране. Серьёзно воспринимать происходящее игра не предлагает — и в этом её главный посыл.

Геймплей привычный для point-and-click: исследование локаций, диалоги, сбор предметов и решение загадок. Большая часть пазлов решается логично и без особых проблем, но иногда встречаются моменты, где правильное решение угадывается скорее перебором, чем дедукцией. Это не ломает игру, но временами слегка замедляет темп.

Персонажи намеренно карикатурные. Главный герой — далеко не самый приятный человек, и игра этого даже не пытается скрывать. Побочные персонажи тоже скорее для шуток и ситуаций, чем полноценные образы. Тем не менее, диалоги написаны живо и местами действительно заставляют улыбнуться.

Юмор — основа проекта и одновременно его главное испытание. Он грубый, прямолинейный, местами абсурдный и часто строится на повторениях. Если вам такой стиль заходит — играть будет интересно до самого финала. Если нет — лучше пропустите этот проект стороной. 

Визуально игрушка выглядит просто: статичные фоны, минимальная анимация и довольно своеобразный стиль. Супер картинки ждать не стоит, но при этом все работает стабильно. Интерфейс понятный и не мешает процессу.

Упоминания заслуживают достижения. Их много, и часть из них требует внимательного исследования локаций и выполнения необязательных действий. Любителям закрывать игры на 100% будет чем заняться. При этом все достижения можно получить за одно прохождение, что важно. 

В итоге Demetrios — нишевый квест, рассчитанный на любителей жанра и специфического юмора. Это игра не для всех, если вам нравятся классические point-and-click квесты и вы спокойно относитесь к цинизму и абсурду — можно попробовать.

Demetrios – The BIG Cynical Adventure is a point-and-click comedy that wears its irreverence proudly, presenting a deliberately unglamorous protagonist and a story that revels in bad decisions, sarcastic commentary, and gleefully inappropriate humor. Developed and published by COWCAT, the game follows Bjorn Thonen, an antique dealer from Paris whose life is a chaotic blend of laziness, incompetence, and questionable hygiene. When his apartment is robbed and a mysterious artifact disappears, Bjorn is dragged—reluctantly—into an adventure that spans streets, deserts, ancient ruins, and a series of ridiculous mishaps. Rather than framing him as a misunderstood genius or a reluctant hero with a hidden heart of gold, the game fully embraces Bjorn’s mediocrity. He is a comic disaster, and the narrative gains much of its charm from watching him stumble his way through a mystery that is clearly beyond him.

The tone of Demetrios is unapologetically crude, cynical, and playful. The game constantly breaks the fourth wall, mocks genre conventions, and uses Bjorn’s own shortcomings as a consistent punchline. Its humor ranges from slapstick to sarcastic commentary, with moments of dark comedy thrown in to keep players off-balance. Even simple interactions—examining objects, speaking to strangers, or making choices—often result in unexpected jokes or grim outcomes. Death screens are numerous and intentionally absurd, encouraging players to experiment even when the consequences are fatal. This humor-first approach gives the game a distinct personality and sets it apart from more restrained adventure titles that focus on dramatic storytelling or subtle wit. It also means players who prefer dry or understated comedy may find the experience brash, while those who enjoy bold, unfiltered humor will likely find it consistently amusing.

Visually, the game feels like a blend of comic book art and retro adventure aesthetics. Every scene is hand-drawn, giving the environments a bright, slightly exaggerated charm that complements the comedic tone. Characters are expressive in a cartoonish way, and the simple animations help keep the focus on narrative and puzzle-solving rather than spectacle. The user interface is intentionally straightforward: classic point-and-click mechanics form the backbone of the experience, with inventory management, hotspot searching, and contextual interactions shaping progression. This adherence to traditional design is both a strength and a limitation. It provides genre fans with an interface they will immediately understand, but it also means the game rarely pushes beyond established conventions of the mid-1990s adventure era.

The puzzle design reflects that same retro sensibility. Most puzzles rely on a familiar chain of acquiring items, interpreting clues, and combining objects in sometimes absurd ways to progress. At its best, this leads to moments of genuine satisfaction when strange solutions click into place; at its worst, it results in the kind of obscure logic leaps that the genre is infamous for. The hint system creatively tied to hidden cookies offers a smart middle ground. Players who get stuck can consume these collectible cookies for increasingly direct hints, while completionists may take pleasure in finding them scattered across nearly every screen. However, the cookie hunts can grow repetitive, and players who dislike pixel-hunting may find this mechanic more of an obligation than a delight.

In terms of pacing, Demetrios strikes a comfortable balance between narrative and exploration. The adventure spans several chapters, each with its own setting, cast of eccentric characters, and tone shifts. Despite its humorous framing, the story maintains a clear sense of progression, and the mysteries surrounding the stolen artifact provide enough intrigue to carry the player from one region to the next. The game is neither overwhelmingly long nor too brief; most players will finish it in around ten hours, depending on puzzle-solving speed and how thoroughly they explore optional interactions. The relatively contained scale helps the game avoid the bloat that sometimes affects modern adventure titles, though it also means it doesn’t offer the branching complexity or dynamic choices seen in narrative-heavy games.

Ultimately, Demetrios – The BIG Cynical Adventure succeeds by knowing exactly what it wants to be: an old-school point-and-click game with a loud, cheeky personality and a refusal to take anything seriously—not even itself. Its appeal hinges almost entirely on tone and writing; those who enjoy cynical humor, eccentric characters, and deliberately unrefined protagonists will have a great time. Those who expect sophisticated puzzles, innovative mechanics, or high-budget production values may find the experience uneven. But within its niche, Demetrios delivers a distinctive, memorable adventure crafted with enthusiasm, self-awareness, and a willingness to embrace the bizarre. It's a quirky, foul-mouthed romp that stands out precisely because it refuses to play by the rules of the genre it affectionately parodies.

[h1]🧐 My Opinion 🧐[/h1]
Demetrios is clearly the work of a solo indie, and it shows – but in a good way. The graphics are amateurish but in the noble sense of the word: not polished like a pro studio, but full of passion. The humor is very French, silly and sometimes crude, with a lot of toilet jokes. It’s not hilarious but it’s lighthearted and goofy enough to work most of the time. There’s even an option to tone down the gross-out jokes, which some people will appreciate. Personally I was fine with it, even if the frequency sometimes felt a bit too high.

The story is simple but coherent: an everyday situation that turns into a quirky adventure. It isn’t gripping, but it flows well enough and holds together as a whole, except for a rushed last quarter and a clumsy detour in [spoiler]Germany[/spoiler]. The game is easy to get into, puzzles are accessible and not frustrating, and the overall rhythm is good. It’s more about relaxing and smiling than really challenging your brain.

The cookie system is a great idea: searching for them feels like a hidden object mini-game, and they work perfectly as hints. When I got stuck on a couple of ocassions, they nudged me in the right direction without spoiling anything. The only real issue is the last part of the game, which feels rushed, with puzzles that are confusing, out of place, and sometimes overly difficult compared to the rest. Luckily, the ending is fine and avoids ending the game on a bad note.

The jokes are rarely brilliant, sometimes even borderline sexist or racist, more crass than witty. Still, the absurd and cynical tone fits the game and reminded me of Monkey Island or Leisure Suit Larry, but dirtier. And contrary to what many reviews say, the protagonist isn’t just a complete idiot: he’s mainly doing absurd or disgusting things (like eating cookies found in vomit). Most of the plans you execute in the game come from him, and while they’re ludicrous, they’re consistent with the game’s world rather than signs of sheer stupidity.

Overall, I got what I wanted: dumb French humor, a light adventure, and a coherent package. It’s not a masterpiece, but in a genre that’s almost dead today, it’s refreshing. If you’re curious and can live with rough edges, give it a try.

It took me a bit less 10 hours, without rushing to beat the game.

[h1]💖 Pros 💖[/h1]
-    Passion project feel, with charm despite amateur graphics

-    Unique tone, reminiscent of classic adventures but dirtier
-    Protagonist’s absurd plans fit the world and aren’t just “idiotic”

[h1]💀 Cons 💀[/h1]
-    Crude humor can feel excessive and not for everyone (but there's an option to tune it down)
-    Last quarter feels rushed, with confusing, out-of-place and overly difficult puzzles
-    Some jokes are more crass than witty

A mediocre point and click game filled with toilet humor. You play as 20 something antique shop owner who hasn't matured past first grade who gets involved with murderous plunderers who try to raid a Middle Eastern secret to find unbelievable treasure who has a crush on his next door bimbo neighbor who's  still better because she's kind and her "special" child bordering on autism (who's mostly insufferable because the main characters are idiots).

The big issue with the game is that there's nothing to keep the player invested in the game. The plot has dozens of holes, and nothing really engages me in the treasure murder mystery plot. The art is indifferent. The 48 game unique game over endings aren't fun to find and is annoying to try to get (thank god cowcat's other game Brok the investigator doesn't have this). Playing as a ignorant buffoon who refuses to read can be fun to watch but is hardly engaging as the main playable character. 

This game also actually has so much toilet humor if you want 100% completion you have to endure all of it. 

Oh and the title? Barely relates to game outside an in game reference. Nothing related to Demetrius, Latinzaed form of the devotees of the Greek Goddess Demeter. Nothing Cynical. Certainly big if you also want to  spend 8 hours like me completionist because you strive for it too. 

If you're like me, you bought this because you loved Brok the Investigator. And if you did, this is Cowcat Game's much earlier much worse first work. You can see a lot of the game engine and narrative input from Brok here, and that's the only reason you might play it. You can also see the many improvements Brok made to this, from having achievements easier to accomplish, hiring outside to design characters while the in-house staff continues those pleasant backgrounds, etc.  

The only reason I grinded 8 hours through this is because I have a habit of trying to completionist all my games and was such a fan of Cowcat's other game Brok the Investigator and got this bundled together. I suppose a good thing is that nothing in the game was so bad it repulsed me away. Besides a few toilet humor scenes, there was nothing awful. 

If you still want to try to this game, take my advice, begin with all the toilet humor and try to grind through the game in no more than 2. It's still a decent point and click and The game has been streamed in under two hours. Otherwise prepare to grind around 8 hours playing throug the game 2.5 times like me for achievements. In all, the big bad thing is it's not good but not bad either.

Бьёрн Тонен, владелец антикварного магазина, коллекционер шоколадного печенья и просто критический идиoт. К несчастью для этого прекрасного, но очень невезучего человека, у него есть древняя статуя большой птицы, статуя необычная и история её происхождения покрыта завесой тайны, но в одну злосчастную ночь у Бьёрна крадут скрижаль находящуюся на этой самой статуе. 
С этой проблемой нашему главному герою и придётся разбираться, встречая на своём пути множество интересных личностей, которые обманут его, оскорбят, посадят за решётку или попросту убьют, хотя с последним мистер Тонен справиться и один.

От себя же скажу, что провёл в игре 10 увлекательных часов. И да, сортирный юмор это класс! В игре кстати есть функция, где можно уменьшить его количество или вовсе выключить, но тогда спрашивается зачем вообще играть в неё. Помимо сортирного юмора, есть ещё несколько панчлайнов про гомосексуалистов, женщин и коренных народов, ну и ещё море стереотипного юмора. Всё это создаёт потрясающий аромат и невероятное послевкусие французского помёта.
Когда шутки заканчиваются, приходит время детектива и с этим всё на самом деле хорошо, вышеперечисленный аромат вкупе с расследованием разбойного ограбления увлекает и хочется продолжать эту историю, хоть и финальный твист угадывается буквально на первых двух часах игры, а вторая половина провисает.

В конце хотелось бы сообщить вам, что может эта история и была циничной, но Бьёрн Тонен таким не является, он всего лишь хотел простого-человеческого счастья.
Покойся с миром, Бьёрн.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

pros

✅ cartoony, colorful and cute hand drawn background artwork and character models
✅ humorous and cartoony story with some surprises about an antique dealer and shop owner getting involved with murderous treasure plunderers who try to find and raid a Middle Eastern temple that has a massive treasure and the ability to grant three wishes of adventurers who find and pass it's traps. In these adventures, his blonde love interest and her annoying child accompany and help him.
✅ there are some nice variety puzzles and mini games. there are also some inventory-based puzzles to solve, so you can also make multiple combinations in your inventory and create new items
✅ colorful, diverse, humorous, goofy and quirky main and side characters
✅ catchy soundtrack fits the game's humorous tone
✅ there are steam achievements and cards
✅ there are some funny dialogues between characters.
✅ there is a hint system that helps you when you are stuck
✅ when you press space, it shows all hotspots, so there are pixel hunting
✅ two playable character
✅ decent length
✅ there is a quick travel map, which prevents backtracking and long walking
✅ there are plenty of different, good-looking, and colorful places
✅ there is auto save

cons

❌ mostly unnecessary, exhausting, and lengthy dialogues between characters
❌ considering all these unnecessary and lengthy dialogues, the lack of voiceovers makes the reading of all these dialogues unbearable and boring.
❌there are too many clickable red herring items to drag out the gameplay, and it's worse that when you click on them, characters make long comments about them.
❌ there are some nonsensical puzzle solutions.
❌ overall tone, dialogues and humor very juvenile, gross, and crude, so it may not appeal to everyone. 
❌ little girl can be so bratty, sarcastic, and annoying. main character and his love interest are also totall imbeciles. I'm sure some people will find them annoying and unlikeable.
